title: Git is not GitHub
concept: git vs GitHub; make the first repository page and a README

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: So far everything lived on your laptop only. Nobody else can see it.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Git is the program on your computer. It saves versions.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: A website like CodeHub stores a copy online so teammates can get it.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Look at the website panel. I already made an empty page for our festival project.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Every project needs a README. It tells people what the project is.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Write README.md on your laptop, then commit it. We will send it online next level.

items.text: Answer: what does the website add that git alone does not?

hints: Make a file called README.md, then stage and commit it like any other file.
The editor panel can create files. Or use `echo` to write one line into README.md.
Run `echo "The Lantern Labs festival website" > README.md`, then `git add README.md`, then `git commit -m "Add README"`.

questions.prompt: You have been committing for five chapters. What can git on your laptop NOT do by itself?

choices.text: Let a teammate on another computer get your work

questions.explanation: Git saves history locally. A hosting website is what makes that history reachable by other people.

recap: Git runs on your computer. A site like CodeHub keeps a copy online so other people can get your work.

solution.run: echo "The Lantern Labs festival website" > README.md
